learn.title: Everything is matter
learn.body: Matter is anything that takes up space and has mass. Air, water, your phone and you are all matter.

learn.title: Three common states
learn.body: A solid keeps its own shape and volume. A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container. A gas spreads out to fill any container.

learn.title: Why they differ
learn.body: It comes down to particles and how much they move. In a solid they are packed tight and only vibrate. In a liquid they slide past each other. In a gas they zoom around with lots of space between them.

learn.title: Changing state
learn.body: Heating and cooling change the state of water.
steps: Ice melts into water at $0\,^\circ\text{C}$ (solid to liquid).
Water boils into steam at $100\,^\circ\text{C}$ at sea level (liquid to gas).
Steam condenses back into water when it cools, and water freezes back into ice.

learn.title: The water cycle
learn.body: The same water goes round and round.
steps: Heat from the sun makes water evaporate.
The vapor rises, cools and condenses into clouds.
Rain falls and collects, ready to start again.

learn.title: Chemical formulas
learn.body: A formula says which atoms a substance has. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom. The small number after a symbol counts its atoms, so $\text{CO}_2$ has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen, and $\text{O}_2$ is two oxygen atoms.
Melting and freezing are opposites. So are evaporation and condensation.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter keeps its shape and its volume?
questions.explanation: Particles in a solid are packed tightly and only vibrate in place.

questions.prompt: Water boils at how many degrees Celsius at sea level?
questions.explanation: At sea level, water boils at $100\,^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.prompt: Ice turning into water is called \_\_.
questions.explanation: Solid to liquid is melting. The reverse is freezing.

questions.prompt: Match each formula with its substance.
questions.explanation: The subscript counts atoms of the element before it.

questions.prompt: Put the water cycle in order.
questions.explanation: Heat lifts water up, cooling forms clouds, and gravity brings it back.
